prompt: Some people think that schools should teach students financial management, while others believe that this is unnecessary. Discuss both views.
essay:
Financial literacy plays a vital role in life regardless of age and gender. While some argue that it should be taught at school, others believe that it can be acquired through personal experiences. This essay will discuss both views.

Some people advocate that learning how to manage money effectively should be a part of the school curriculum to make the most of it. Provided that young students can grasp the foundation of financial education in schools, they will have chances to experiment this and learn from their mistakes. For example, in some schools, a small market is open where young students can buy and sell snacks so as to apply the financial knowledge they have learnt. Additionally, learning about budgeting, saving and responsible spending in early years will shape them to become financially responsible in adulthood. Without having to learn the lesson the hard way, future generations can make informed financial decisions in their lives, which can bring a lot more benefits to the country’s economy.

On the other hand, it is suggested that financial literacy can be easily developed in adult life through real-life experiences. Whether setting up their own business or working in corporate chains, adults will get a taste of financial knowledge and figure it out on their own. The older generations are a prime example of it. Even though there was no formal education in finance, some managed to budget their income well by learning from their mistakes. Moreover, they can receive financial guidance from their seniors and family members, as they can share hands-on experiences which are feasible for the real world. Also, there is no one-size-fits-all strategy, the life lessons and experiences while working can equip them with essential survival life skills.

In conclusion, structured education can help young people acquire proper money-handling skills, whereas practical financial management can be gained through personal experiences. Both approaches have their own advantages and it is a matter of perspective.
